clue.text: Talk among experts includes changes in ardour

indicators.note: in tells us the rearranged letters go inside the synonym for ardour

parts.note: ardour is passion

indicators.note: changes tells us the letters of the word includes are rearranged

explanation.surface: A specialists' talk turns on how heated feelings shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'includes' looks like a container signal but is the anagram fodder, rearranged by 'changes'; 'in' then splits the synonym for ardour around those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A discussion held by a panel of specialists is literally talk among experts, often before an audience.

clue.text: Now 10 27 arrival includes headless bust

indicators.note: includes tells us the trimmed word sits inside the word for arrival

parts.note: an arrival is a comer, one who comes

indicators.note: headless means the word bust loses its first letter

parts.note: taken as written before its head is removed

explanation.surface: A newcomer arriving today brings a broken bust with its head off.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 is TRAIN and 27 is PASSENGER: rail companies now call train passengers 'customers', hence 'Now'.
explanation.definitionFit: Modern railway announcements refer to people travelling on a train as customers rather than passengers.

clue.text: See 23
"Very cold" and "largely clear" — follows time right for vehicle

indicators.note: follows says the cold and clear pieces come after time and right

parts.note: very cold means icy

indicators.note: largely means most of the word clear is kept, its last letters dropped

parts.note: taken as written before its end is cut

explanation.surface: A weather report, icy and mostly clear, introduces a vehicle at the right time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'largely' drops the AR of CLEAR, leaving CLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-wheeled cycle is a simple human-powered vehicle, often a child's first.

clue.text: Accent on foot?

definitions.meaning: a ... is a regional accent, especially an Irish one
a sturdy shoe, worn on the foot

explanation.definitionFit: Brogue names both a lilting regional accent and a stout leather shoe with decorative punched holes.

clue.text: I remove greater objects from s-shoe

parts.note: the clue's s is taken as written
a trainer is a sports shoe

explanation.surface: Something boasting it can pick big items out of a stammered shoe.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition speaks in the first person: a sieve-like device keeps back larger pieces and lets the rest through.
explanation.definitionFit: A strainer is a mesh utensil that holds back larger solids while letting liquid pass through.

clue.text: Fish on line in part of flower

indicators.note: in a down clue the fish sits on top of the line

parts.note: a carp is a freshwater fish
an el is an elevated railway line in American cities

explanation.surface: A fish hooked on a line beside a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: EL, the elevated railway, suits the puzzle's train theme.
explanation.definitionFit: The carpel is the female reproductive organ of a flower, holding the ovules.

clue.text: Russian princess out of Asia, 2B if out in English city, unpleasant character

indicators.note: out of means the word Asia is removed from the princess's name

parts.note: Anastasia was the youngest daughter of the last Tsar
taken as written, to be removed

indicators.note: in puts the scrambled letters inside the city

parts.note: York is a cathedral city in the north of England

indicators.note: out means the letters of 2B and if are scrambled

parts.note: 2B spelt out is TWO B, followed by if as written

explanation.surface: A missing Russian princess turns up in York, and she is trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' strips ASIA from the princess, 'out' scrambles TWOBIF into BITOFW, and 'in' puts that inside the city; 'out' appears twice with two different jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: A nasty bit of work is an idiom for a spiteful or unpleasant person.

clue.text: Sinner, a boring enemy of Bush, said to be badly stressed

indicators.note: said with the stress in the wrong place, the phrase runs together into a single word

parts.note: a dull terror: a boring foe of the kind George W Bush's war on terror targeted

explanation.surface: A sinner, a tedious foe of President Bush, is said to be under stress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a dull terror', spoken with the stress misplaced, comes out as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Adultery is traditionally counted a sin, so one who commits it is a sinner.

clue.text: Followers maybe in tube

definitions.meaning: a retinue of attendants following an important person
a ... runs in the London Underground tube

explanation.definitionFit: Train means both a retinue following a dignitary and a line of railway carriages, such as those in the tube.

clue.text: City theme in tube?

parts.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London
a theme is a topic

explanation.surface: A city's theme, whether on the London Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tube' is the Fallopian tube, the commonest site of an ectopic pregnancy, not the Underground of 10.
explanation.definitionFit: An ectopic pregnancy develops outside the womb, most often in a Fallopian tube.

clue.text: Good animal, the Manx cat — could be a killer

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep

indicators.note: a Manx cat has no tail, so the word for cat loses its last letter

parts.note: puss is a familiar word for a cat

explanation.surface: A good animal, the tailless Manx cat, might be a killer.
explanation.definitionFit: Grampus is an old name for the killer whale, and also for Risso's dolphin.

clue.text: Mother's name for malediction

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother

explanation.surface: Mother's word for a curse.
explanation.definitionFit: To damn someone is to curse them, so the word serves as a malediction or oath.

clue.text: Film text is Lean's with Percy co-operating

indicators.note: co-operating suggests the letters working together in a new arrangement

parts.note: the possessive's S is needed here: LEANS

explanation.surface: Director David Lean's script is a joint effort with someone called Percy.
explanation.walkthrough: David Lean was the director of Lawrence of Arabia.
explanation.definitionFit: A screenplay is the written script of a film, with dialogue and directions.

clue.text: Worship tree now added to 10

definitions.meaning: the ... tree is a European tree related to the rowan

explanation.definitionFit: Service names a church act of worship, the sorb or service tree, and a scheduled train in railway jargon.

clue.text: Cross boundary where some festivities occur

definitions.meaning: to overstep a limit or rule
fringe festivals, like Edinburgh's, run beside main ones

explanation.definitionFit: To infringe is to break a rule or cross a line; read as two words it locates fringe festival events.

clue.text: Last 3s for 10 with a lot of fur in it otherwise

indicators.note: in tells us the trimmed fur goes inside the rearranged letters
otherwise means the letters of it are put another way
a lot of means most of the fur word, its final letter dropped

parts.note: ermine is the white winter fur of the stoat

explanation.surface: Final stops for a train, wrapped in plenty of fur.
explanation.walkthrough: 3 is STOP and 10 is TRAIN, cross-references to other answers. 'otherwise' turns IT into TI; 'a lot of' drops the fur's final letter; 'in' sets it between the T and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Termini are the end points of rail lines, the last stopping places for trains.

clue.text: Pampas is where novel girl is about to dance

indicators.note: about tells us the girl's name goes round the dance

parts.note: Tess of the d'Urbervilles is Thomas Hardy's novel
a reel is a lively Scottish folk dance

explanation.surface: On the South American grasslands a fictional heroine is about to dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The pampas are vast South American grassy plains with few or no trees.

clue.text: Way of thinking supplies good lie for your head

indicators.note: supplies, read as makes supple, bends the letters of good lie into a new shape
head picks out the first letter of your

explanation.surface: A worldview hands out a convenient untruth in place of your own mind.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideology is a system of beliefs and ideas, a characteristic way of thinking.

clue.text: Natural and unnatural duet about vulgar City

indicators.note: about tells us the rearranged letters wrap round the next pieces
unnatural signals that the letters of duet appear in an unnatural order

parts.note: naff is British slang for tasteless or vulgar
EC is the postcode of the City of London

explanation.surface: A singing pair, contrived and set against a crass financial district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Natural and unnatural' sits as a playful contrast: the first is the definition, the second only the anagram signal. 'about' puts the rearranged UTED round the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Unaffected describes manner that is natural and sincere, without pretence.

clue.text: A tax on a right to an image

parts.note: VAT is value added tax

explanation.surface: A levy on a legal entitlement to one's picture.
explanation.definitionFit: An avatar is an embodiment or icon, an image representing someone, as online.

clue.text: Has 26 the ability to snack?

parts.note: can expresses having the ability
26 is ORANG, an orang-utan, which is an ape

explanation.surface: Is a monkey able to eat between meals?
explanation.definitionFit: A canape is a small savoury bite served with drinks, a snack.

clue.text: At the end endless love comes to nothing

parts.note: Z is the end of the alphabet

indicators.note: endless means the word for love loses its last letter

parts.note: Eros is the Greek god of love

explanation.surface: In the end a love affair without limits amounts to nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Zero is the number nought, standing for nothing at all.

clue.text: Issues about pantomimist are ahead of tautology in announcement on 10

indicators.note: are ahead of puts the first part before the second
about tells us the offspring word wraps round the mime artist

parts.note: issue means offspring, here a son
Jacques Tati was a French mime and comic film-maker
the second word adds nothing to the first, which is the tautology

explanation.surface: Children circling a mime artist precede a redundant phrase in a train announcement.
explanation.walkthrough: The full phrase heard on British trains, 'next station stop', is mocked as a tautology, since station and the second word mean the same thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Train conductors announce each approaching halt with this stock phrase, naming the next stopping point.

clue.text: Killed as Brer Fox didn't need to be?

definitions.text: as Brer Fox didn't need to be?
definitions.meaning: in the Tar-Baby tale Brer Fox 'lay low', lying hidden; he lay low himself

explanation.definitionFit: Laid low means felled or killed, and plays on the Brer Rabbit refrain about Brer Fox lying low.

clue.text: Couple commonly suggesting they should be assaulted

indicators.note: commonly suggests a dropped aitch, as in casual London speech

parts.note: hit 'em means strike them

explanation.surface: A pair whose name implies they deserve a beating.
explanation.definitionFit: An item is a romantic couple, as in 'they are an item'.

clue.text: Primate or spirit missing some electricity

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: missing tells us part of the electricity word is taken out of the spirit

parts.note: an angel is a spirit
the opening letters of electricity, E and L

explanation.surface: An ape, or a ghost cut off from part of the power supply.
explanation.definitionFit: An orang, short for orang-utan, is a great ape of Borneo and Sumatra, a primate.

clue.text: Return of Cape grapefruit maybe coming round for one on 10

indicators.note: coming round says the scrambled fruit wraps round the reversed headland
maybe signals the letters of the fruit are not in their usual order

parts.note: grape, the fruit at the front of the word

indicators.note: return of says the headland word is read backwards

parts.note: a ness is a cape or headland

explanation.surface: South African grapefruit coming back round, perhaps for someone on a train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return of' gives SSEN; 'maybe' turns GRAPE into PAGER, which 'coming round' wraps about it. 'grapefruit' reads as one word but only its first half is used. 10 is TRAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A passenger is someone travelling on a train who is not part of its crew.
